### Overview
- Last updated: 2026_07_23
- Based on: 2 answer scripts in `.github/answers/` (2024_08_20, 2025_02_10)
- Overall level: intermediate (around CEFR B1). Can develop familiar topics at length with concrete examples, but accuracy in basic grammar (tense, articles) is unstable.

<br>

### Strengths
- Develops stories at length with concrete examples and reasons on topics of interest (tech, cooking, daily life).
- Broad vocabulary within familiar topics (e.g. "converted into digital vectors", "automated systems").
- Attempts self-correction by rephrasing into more natural sentences (e.g. "people utterly mistake me..." → "people mistakenly think...").
- Proactive learner: asks for feedback on tense and word choice.

<br>

### Weaknesses
- Tense consistency: present tense mixes into past-tense stories (e.g. "i just wonder about" → wondered).
- Missing articles: frequently drops the/a (e.g. "internet isn't spread widely" → the internet).
- Double comparatives: stacks "more" onto comparatives (e.g. "more lower pitch" → a lower pitch).
- Preposition/verb choice: direct translations from Korean (e.g. "mail to you" → mailed you, "by internet" → over the internet).
- Falls back to Korean when stuck (e.g. "전에 한번은 i just wonder...").
- Sentence fragments: incomplete sentences without a verb (e.g. "Not that any special motivated things.").

<br>

### Priority Focus
- Keep past-tense consistency when talking about past experiences (first priority).
- Build the habit of deciding whether a noun needs an article (the/a).

<br>

### Maintenance Rules
- Update this analysis and the "Last updated" date every time feedback is given on a new answer script.
- When a weakness no longer appears, remove it from Weaknesses and reflect it in Strengths.
